simple.biblicalBackground: The first appearances are in Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, and 17 more, beginning at Genesis 12:10. BibleIQ detects the main surrounding context as family, family line, flock, land, Egypt.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to גּוּר (H1481) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: People in Scripture are understood by their place in the story. BibleIQ follows גּוּר through the actual verses so the reader sees the person in context instead of as an isolated dictionary entry.
simple.summary: גּוּר (gûwr) / H1481 is tracked through Genesis 12:10, Genesis 19:9, Genesis 20:1, Genesis 21:23. The entry is generated from source alignment, occurrence evidence, and the surrounding Scripture context.

They said, “Stand back!” Then they said, “This one fellow came in to live as a foreigner, and he appoints himself a judge. Now we will deal worse with you than with them!” They pressed hard on the man Lot, and came near to break the door.
Abraham traveled from there toward the land of the South, and lived between Kadesh and Shur. He lived as a foreigner in Gerar.

Now, therefore, swear to me here by God that you will not deal falsely with me, nor with my son, nor with my son’s son. But according to the kindness that I have done to you, you shall do to me, and to the land in which you have lived as a foreigner.”

They also said to Pharaoh, “We have come to live as foreigners in the land, for there is no pasture for your servants’ flocks. For the famine is severe in the land of Canaan. Now therefore, please let your servants dwell in the land of Goshen.”

I have also established my covenant with them, to give them the land of Canaan, the land of their travels, in which they lived as aliens.

When a stranger lives as a foreigner with you, and would like to keep the Passover to Yahweh, let all his males be circumcised, and then let him come near and keep it. He shall be as one who is born in the land; but no uncircumcised person shall eat of it.
One law shall be to him who is born at home, and to the stranger who lives as a foreigner among you.”
